title: Solomon’s merchants received “linen yarn” — the Greek of 2 Chronicles has no yarn
summary: The KJV says the king’s merchants received “linen yarn” at a price. The Hebrew prints one word, מִקְוֵא, twice, and Brenton’s Greek of 2 Chronicles 1:16 names no goods at all. Brenton’s Greek of 1 Kings 10:28 reads the same place as “from Thekoue”.
text: KJV 2 Chronicles 1:16: “And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price.” Hebrew (WLC) 1:16: וּמֹוצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕א סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מִקְוֵ֥א יִקְח֖וּ בִּמְחִֽיר׃ [and the bringing out of the horses that Solomon had from Egypt, and the miqwe; the king’s traders took the miqwe at a price]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Chronicles 1:16: Καὶ ἡ ἔξοδος τῶν ἵππων Σαλωμὼν ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἡ τιμὴ τῶν ἐμπόρων τοῦ βασιλέως πορεύεσθαι, καὶ ἠγόραζον [and the export of Solomon’s horses from Egypt, and the price of the king’s merchants for going, and they bought]. Brenton English: “and the charge of the king's merchants for going was as follows, and they traded”. KJV 1 Kings 10:28: “And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Kings 10:28: וּמֹוצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕ה סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יִקְח֥וּ מִקְוֵ֖ה בִּמְחִֽיר׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Kings 10:28: Καὶ ἡ ἔξοδος Σαλωμῶν τῶν ἱππέων καὶ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἐκ Θεκουὲ ἔμποροι τοῦ βασιλέως· καὶ ἐλάμβανον ἐκ Θεκουὲ ἐν ἀλλάγματι [and the export of Solomon’s horsemen, also from Egypt, and from Thekoue the king’s merchants; and they took from Thekoue in exchange]. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2CH01.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI10.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/1/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/10/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH01.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI10.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2CH01.htm.
reasoning: In the KJV the second item bought in Egypt beside horses is “linen yarn”, a commodity. The Hebrew has the word מִקְוֵא (2 Chronicles) or מִקְוֵה (1 Kings) in the same slot, twice in each verse. Brenton’s Greek of 2 Chronicles 1:16 has no word for goods there: the traders’ “price” and “going” appear, and nothing is said to be received. Brenton’s Greek of 1 Kings 10:28 has the name Θεκουέ, a place from which the merchants came. The Greek therefore gives either no goods (Chronicles) or a place (Kings) where the KJV has a commodity.
scope: T applies at 2 Chronicles 1:16, Septuagint only. The record compares what the three texts print. It does not say what the Hebrew word means, whether it names goods or a place, or that “linen yarn” is wrong, and it does not say which Greek rendering is original. A rare word that the KJV renders by one choice and the Greek by another does not by itself show that either is mistaken. The shared verse 1 Kings 10:28 is context: its Greek was compared in an earlier session and not issued, and is quoted here only to show how the same Hebrew was read in the Greek of Kings. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. title: Jeroboam’s priests “for the devils” — the Greek says “for the idols and for the vain things”
summary: The KJV says Jeroboam ordained priests for the high places, “for the devils” and for the calves. Brenton’s Greek has “the idols” and “the vain things”, two nouns for one Hebrew word. The same Hebrew word is the one the KJV renders “goats” in Leviticus 16:8.
text: KJV 2 Chronicles 11:15: “And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:15: וַיַּֽעֲמֶד־לֹו֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים לַבָּמֹ֖ות וְלַשְּׂעִירִ֑ים וְלָעֲגָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃ [and he appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for the seirim, and for the calves that he made]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 11:15: καὶ κατέστησεν ἑαυτῷ ἱερεῖς τῶν ὑψηλῶν καὶ τοῖς εἰδώλοις καὶ τοῖς ματαίοις καὶ τοῖς μόσχοις, ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἱεροβοάμ. [and he appointed for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vain things, and for the calves that Jeroboam made]. Brenton English: “And he made for himself priests of the high places, and for the idols, and for the vanities, and for the calves which Jeroboam made.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2CH11.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/11/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH11.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2CH11.htm.
reasoning: The KJV names the second class served by the priests as “devils”, which are beings. The Hebrew word is הַשְּׂעִירִים, the plural noun that Leviticus 16:8 prints for the two goats and that the published Leviticus 17:7 record already sets beside the KJV’s “devils”. Brenton’s Greek here uses two plural nouns, “the idols” and “the vain things”, and does not call them devils. The Hebrew has one word where the Greek has two.
scope: T applies at 2 Chronicles 11:15, Septuagint only. No Hebrew mistranslation is claimed: the Hebrew noun is the one the KJV renders “goats” elsewhere, but a shared word does not settle its sense here, and it may name beings thought of in goat form. This record compares two printed wordings and does not decide what was worshipped or say that the KJV and Greek disagree about the practice, which both report. It is a sibling of the Leviticus 17:7 record `sacrifices-unto-devils-or-to-vain-things-greek`, at a different verse; the two share no verse. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. title: Jehoiada’s coup: “let none come into the house of the Lord, save the priests” — or captains and the guard brought in?
summary: In 2 Chronicles 23 Jehoiada orders that none enter the house of the Lord except priests and ministering Levites, and the Levites guard the king. In 2 Kings 11 he brings the captains and the guard to himself in the house of the Lord, swears them there, and sets two parts of them to keep its watch.
text: KJV 2 Chronicles 23:4: “This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors;” KJV 23:6: “But let none come into the house of the Lord, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the Lord.” KJV 23:7: “And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out.” KJV 2 Kings 11:4: “And the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the rulers over hundreds, with the captains and the guard, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord, and made a covenant with them, and took an oath of them in the house of the Lord, and shewed them the king's son.” KJV 11:5: “And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you that enter in on the sabbath shall even be keepers of the watch of the king's house;” KJV 11:7: “And two parts of all you that go forth on the sabbath, even they shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord about the king.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Chronicles 23:4: זֶ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֨ית מִכֶּ֜ם בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת לַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְלַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְשֹֽׁעֲרֵ֖י הַסִּפִּֽים׃ [the third of you who come in on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, for gatekeepers of the thresholds]. Hebrew (WLC) 23:6: וְאַל־יָבֹ֣וא בֵית־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י אִם־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַמְשָׁרְתִ֣ים לַלְוִיִּ֔ם הֵ֥מָּה יָבֹ֖אוּ כִּי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֑מָּה [and let none come into the house of the Lord except the priests and the ministers of the Levites; they shall come in, for they are holy]. Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 11:4: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠שְּׁבִיעִית שָׁלַ֨ח יְהֹויָדָ֜ע וַיִּקַּ֣ח ׀ אֶת־שָׂרֵ֣י [הַמֵּאיֹות כ] (הַמֵּאֹ֗ות ק) לַכָּרִי֙ וְלָ֣רָצִ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה [and in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of the hundreds, for the Carites and the runners, and brought them to him, the house of the Lord; the WLC prints both a written (ketiv) and a read (qere) form of “hundreds”]. Hebrew (WLC) 11:5: הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֤ית מִכֶּם֙ בָּאֵ֣י הַשַּׁבָּ֔ת וְשֹׁ֣מְרֵ֔י מִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ [the third of you who come in on the sabbath, and keepers of the watch of the king’s house]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Chronicles 23:6: Καὶ μὴ εἰσελθέτω εἰς οἶκον Κυρίου, ἐὰν μὴ οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ οἱ Λευῖται καὶ οἱ λειτουργοῦντες τῶν Λευιτῶν [and let none enter the house of the Lord unless the priests and the Levites and the ministers of the Levites]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4 Kingdoms (2 Kings) 11:4: Καὶ ἐν τῷ ἔτει τῷ ἑβδόμῳ ἀπέστειλεν Ἰωδαὲ, καὶ ἔλαβε τοὺς ἑκατοντάρχους τῶν Χοῤῥὶ καὶ τῶν Ῥασίμ, καὶ ἀπήγαγεν αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον Κυρίου [and Jehoiada sent and took the centurions of the Chorri and the Rasim, and led them to him into the house of the Lord]. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2CH23.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI11.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/23/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/11/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH23.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI11.htm.
reasoning: The two accounts of the same coup describe the force differently. Chronicles names the third entering on the sabbath as “of the priests and of the Levites”, gatekeepers of the thresholds, forbids anyone else to enter the house of the Lord, and has the Levites compass the king. Kings names the men as the commanders of hundreds with the Carites and the runners (KJV “captains and the guard”), brings them into the house of the Lord, swears them there, assigns a third to the king’s house, and sets “two parts” to keep the watch of the house of the Lord about the king. The gates also differ in name: Kings has “the gate of Sur” and “the gate behind the guard”; Chronicles has “the gate of the foundation” (Brenton: “the middle gate”). One account has only temple personnel inside the house; the other has the armed guard inside it.
scope: Untagged: the KJV, the Hebrew and the Greek agree with each other in each book, and the difference is between the two books. The two can be read together, since 2 Chronicles 23:1 names five captains of hundreds and 23:8 has “the Levites and all Judah” carry out the plan, so the men may have been the same people described in different terms, or the guard may have been posted outside the house. Neither text says so. The record sets the two wordings side by side and does not say either is in error. The Hebrew word for the guard in Kings (הָרָצִים, runners) is not shown to mean Levites. 2 Kings 11 was covered in an earlier session without a record at these verses; this one is issued with the later book under the standing ruling on comparisons across books. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.

title: Uzziah’s burial: “in the field of the burial which belonged to the kings” — or “in the city of David”?
summary: 2 Chronicles says the leprous king was buried with his fathers “in the field of the burial which belonged to the kings”. 2 Kings says Azariah was buried with his fathers “in the city of David”. Both name Jotham as the successor.
text: KJV 2 Chronicles 26:23: “So Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial which belonged to the kings; for they said, He is a leper: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.” KJV 2 Kings 15:7: “So Azariah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Chronicles 26:23: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֨וּ אֹתֹ֤ו עִם־אֲבֹתָיו֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֤ה הַקְּבוּרָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמְּלָכִ֔ים כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ מְצֹורָ֣ע ה֑וּא וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יֹותָ֥ם בְּנֹ֖ו תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ [and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial that belonged to the kings, for they said, He is a leper]. Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 15:7: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב עֲזַרְיָה֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹתֹ֛ו עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יֹותָ֥ם בְּנֹ֖ו תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ [and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Chronicles 26:23: καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ τῆς ταφῆς τῶν βασιλέων, ὅτι εἶπαν ὅτι λεπρός ἐστι [and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial of the kings, because they said he is a leper]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4 Kingdoms (2 Kings) 15:7: καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ ἐν πόλει Δαυὶδ [and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David]. Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2CH26.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI15.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/14/26/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/15/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2CH26.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI15.htm.
reasoning: Both verses report the burial of the king who was succeeded by Jotham and who was buried “with his fathers”. Kings gives the place as the city of David. Chronicles gives it as a field of burial belonging to the kings, and adds the reason, that he was a leper. The Hebrew and the Greek read as the KJV does in both books. 2 Kings 15:1 calls the king Azariah and 2 Chronicles 26:1 calls him Uzziah; the two chapters give the same reign length (fifty-two years) and the same successor.
scope: Untagged: the KJV, the Hebrew and the Greek agree with each other in each book. The two descriptions are not shown to be incompatible: the field of the burial that belonged to the kings may lie in or beside the city of David, and “with his fathers” is said in both. Neither text locates the field. The record sets the two wordings side by side and does not say that either is in error. That Azariah and Uzziah are one king rests on the shared reign length and successor in the two chapters and is not stated in one verse.
